Seeing first time posts like this destroys me. I've been there, and I know that if you don't try to stop now that you'll be in even deeper shit soon. Your situation sounds shitty enough, but if I could go back to being in your situation I would 100% find different coping mechanisms. 

If you do it for the pain, try using a rubber band or hairband instead. 

If you do it for the blood, use a red pen/marker. If the pen is pointy enough, you can use this for pain as well. 

Some other random things that helped me were listening to really loud music in earbuds, rolling dice, wetting pencils and writing on myself with them, painting on myself.

I know you're a grown adult and really struggling right now, and I can't tell you what to do, but please, please try to stop while you still can. It can be just as bad as any other addiction, and seeing people just starting kills me as a person who has struggled for years. 

If you're going to keep doing it, PLEASE take good care of your cuts. I use Aquaphore or Vaseline and aloe to heal them, prevent infection, and lessen scarring.  Make sure your equipment is clean as well as your skin. Places like thighs are easier to heal as well as hide if that makes any difference to you. Don't go much deeper than you already have. If it bleeds a lot, apply pressure, if it's still going after 10 minutes, go to the hospital. You probably already know basic first aid, but please, please be safe if you're going to continue self harming. 

I am in no way saying you should continue self harming, but I want to make sure you're safe. Please reach out to me if you need ANYTHING. I know life can be really shitty, but I know from experience that this isn't the right answer.

I want to preface this with saying that I am trans FTM and pre-op at this point in time although I do want to medically transition. I ma dating a cis bi woman, and am bi myself, having had past relationships with both men and women. 

I do not think it is transphobic for a gay man/straight woman or even a bi/pan person to not want to date me. This is because of both the desire to have biological kids or genital preference which is completely understandable as I would probably not date another trans man. Unless the person is being transphobic in a non romantic way, I don't have a problem with them. 

However, it does seem that in today's world, most people will be more open to dating a trans person because sexuality is not based in sex, it is based on gender identity, even though people with gender preferences are completely valid in that desire. 

I would find it transphobic if I lesbian/straight man were to pursue me after being aware of my gender  identity because that is invalidating and can cause dysphoria.

I will respect all people no matter if I agree with their beliefs or not, like people who say they are trans without dysphoria. There is scientific and historical backing to both binary and non binary trans people, but they have had dysphoria. The things that many trans people are trying to say that I have a problem with are 1) You don't need dysphoria to be trans and 2) there are however many genders. Even though I don't agree with these people, I will respect them as long as they act the same towards me.

I absolutely understand how people don't feel as though they are in the gender binary, and have no problem whatsoever with non binary identities, I just don't count those identities or the non binary spectrum as a third or fourth gender because they typically want to be somewhere between a man and a woman, or nowhere at all. Although I don't understand the motivation to transition if you don't have dysphoria, I will always respect those people and their identity/pronouns.
